content.title: About
content.content: Marshmallow topping is a soft, airy confection made from sugar, glucose syrup, gelatin, and flavorings, designed to sprinkle over desserts, ice cream, drinks, and baked goods. It has a sweet, slightly vanilla taste and a delicate texture that melts in the mouth.

content.title: Interesting Facts
items: The first marshmallow recipe dates back to ancient Egypt, where they used the sap of the mallow plant.
Modern marshmallows began mass production in the United States in the early 1920s thanks to the introduction of gelatin.
Marshmallow topping is often used as a "flaming" garnish for cocktails, where the pieces are briefly set alight.
Colored versions are created by adding food‑grade dyes.
Topping is frequently sold in individually sealed packets for convenience.

items.title: Quick energy source
items.content: The sugar in marshmallow topping is rapidly absorbed, providing an immediate energy boost.

items.title: Easy to eat
items.content: Its soft texture makes it suitable for children and people with chewing difficulties.

items.title: Mood enhancement
items.content: Sweet flavors can stimulate serotonin production, helping improve mood.

items.title: High sugar content
items.content: Large amounts of sugar may contribute to weight gain and increase the risk of dental caries.

items.title: Gelatin allergy
items.content: Some individuals may be allergic to gelatin used in marshmallows.

items.title: Not vegan-friendly
items.content: Traditional marshmallow topping contains animal‑derived gelatin, so vegans should choose plant‑based alternatives.

content.title: How to Eat
content.content: Marshmallow topping can be sprinkled over ice cream, yogurt, hot chocolate, pancakes, waffles, and used in baking and desserts. It can also be briefly toasted over an open flame for a caramelized flavor.

content.title: Storage
content.content: Store the topping in an airtight container in a cool, dry place away from direct sunlight. For longer shelf life, keep it in the refrigerator to prevent softening from humidity.
